newsitem.title: UK: Open skies deal may be on hold til election - paper.
newsitem.headline: Open skies deal may be on hold til election - paper.

text.p: An open skies agreement between the UK and U.S. , aimed at liberalising transatlantic air traffic, may not be finalised until after the election, industry executives believe, said the Financial Times on Thursday.

The UK election must be held by May 22 at the latest. If there is a delay it would also hold back approval for the proposed transatlantic alliance between British Airways and American Airlines. Open skies is a pre-condition for clearing the deal.
The deal will also come under renewed attack from United Airlines vice-president Cyril Murphy at a London conference later Thursday.
He is due to make a speech claiming that BA and American plan to link up with Japan Airlines to create an "iron triangle" which would dominate air traffic in the U.S., Europe and Asia, said the FT.
BA and American were reported to have refused to comment on this.
On open skies itself, the report says no new date has been set for talks, but airline executives believe that negotiations could resume in the summer after an election is out of the way.
